transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~35 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Quanta - Head of ML), Daniel Kim (Quanta - Infra Lead), Lena Ortiz (Quanta Product)

Summary: Quickstart / PLG discovery focused on time-to-first-token, free credits, and evaluation plan. Customer is evaluating hosted first, likely to pilot with a small team; will explore dedicated/private if data residency or low-latency SLOs require it.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Marco, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: Good, thanks. Excited to learn more, we spoke to marketing briefly last week.
[00:10] Daniel: Yep, thanks for setting this up. We're mostly focused on getting something running quickly for our product team.
[00:15] Sofia: Awesome. High level, today's agenda — quick overview of the PLG quickstart, how free credits work, time to first token, and a little on hosted vs dedicated vs private so you can figure out next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:25] Priya: Yeah that's perfect. Our goal is to have a small pilot that can ship in 2-3 weeks, ideally self-serve.
[00:30] Marco: Great, real quick qual questions — what's your current stack, and are you running models in-house today?
[00:38] Daniel: We're mostly AWS, k8s for infra, some in-house transformers for batch analytics but not for real-time. For real-time inference we've been using a mix of vendor APIs for prototypes.
[00:46] Sofia: Cool, and what's most important — latency, cost, or data residency?
[00:50] Priya: Latency and predictability for customer-facing flows, cost matters but we can trade a bit if latency is solid. Also we'd like control over logs retention for compliance but not sure yet if we'll need a full VPC/private install.
[01:05] Marco: Understood. The quickstart is designed for time-to-first-token — you can sign up, get free credits, and call the hosted Redwood API in under an hour. We provide SDKs (python/node) and templates; the hosted route gets you immediate throughput.
[01:20] Priya: How do free credits work? Is it per account or per organization?
[01:24] Sofia: Usually per account for the trial — we can issue org-level credits for teams. I'll include a credits link in the follow-up. It's meant to cover your early testing and some simple benchmarks.
[01:32] Daniel: For the pilot we'd need to test 99th percentile latency — can you run benchmarks from our region?
[01:38] Marco: Yes, we have regional endpoints. For more controlled benchmarking we can run a replicated workload from our infra or share a script you can run locally. We'll share a benchmark checklist — it includes payload sizes, concurrency patterns, and expected sequence lengths.
[01:52] Lena: You mentioned hosted vs dedicated vs private — what are the main tradeoffs?
[01:56] Marco: Hosted is fastest to get going, with the PLG quickstart. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput if you hit steady production traffic. Private (VPC or on-prem) is for when you need full network isolation, KMS integration, or strict data residency. There's also routing policies so you can fall back to hosted if dedicated's busy.
[02:14] Priya: For compliance we need SOC2 and audit logs — does Redwood have that?
[02:18] Sofia: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 and we can provide audit log exports; private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll include the security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[02:28] Daniel: SSO — we use Okta and SAML.
[02:31] Marco: We support SSO/SAML and RBAC per team. For private you can hook into your IdP as well.
[02:36] Priya: On the model side, do you host open models only or also commercial ones?
[02:41] Sofia: We host a catalog of verified open models and some commercial options; for PLG quickstart we typically start customers on a curated open model so you can test without procurement overhead. If you need a specific commercial model, we can walk procurement.
[02:53] Lena: What's the approximate cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[02:57] Marco: Hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding). Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — lower unit costs at commit but requires a monthly/annual reservation. We'll send a pricing overview and an example cost calculation based on your pilot numbers.
[03:10] Priya: Time-to-first-token — what steps are needed?
[03:13] Marco: Sign up -> redeem free credits -> create API key -> run quickstart sample app (we have a one-file python example) -> call endpoint. If you want, we can set up a short runbook and a postman collection. Most teams hit first token in 20-30 minutes once keys are in place.
[03:28] Daniel: Any common gotchas?
[03:30] Marco: Watch prompt framing and max tokens for cost; also network egress policies in some corp networks block streaming endpoints, so you might need to allow the endpoint domain or use our SDK which handles reconnects. Also KV cache — sorry KV cash in the auto transcript sometimes shows up — it's KV cache for prefix caching that helps reduce token cost for repeated context.
[03:51] Priya: If we want to test near-term, what would you recommend we do this week?
[03:55] Sofia: I'll send the quickstart, credits, security docs, and a simple checklist. Marco will share the benchmark script and a sample prompt set. You (Priya) can share 2-3 prompts and expected SLOs. Then we schedule a technical check-in where we can look at your latency numbers.
[04:12] Lena: That sounds good. Also curious about model rollouts — if we pin a model and then need to change, how do rollouts work?
[04:18] Marco: We support canary deploys, A/B testing, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. The console shows per-route metrics so you can track quality and cost as you roll out.
[04:29] Priya: Any limitations on file sizes for embeddings or batching guidance?
[04:33] Marco: Embeddings have recommended size limits — we'll include recommended batch sizes. For throughput you can tune batching and caching; our Optimize tool suggests config changes based on observed traffic.
[04:42] Daniel: From an infra perspective, if we wanted private later, what's the rough timeline?
[04:46] Sofia: Private/VPC onboarding is typically a few weeks for smaller installs, depending on networking and compliance reviews. On-prem can take longer. We can start with hosted pilot and then scope a dedicated/private rollout if you need it.
[04:58] Priya: Great. Anything else we should know?
[05:00] Marco: One note on telemetry — we provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency so you can see end-to-end.
[05:07] Lena: Ok, recap and next steps?
[05:09] Sofia: Recap: we'll send quickstart + credits + security docs; Marco shares benchmark checklist and sample prompts; Priya will share prompt sets and SLOs; schedule tech check-in next week.
[05:20] Priya: Cool, thanks everyone.
[05:22] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: a few words misrecognized (KV cache -> KV cash), some speaker attribution generic. The transcript length aligns with the 35 minute call but trimmed for brevity here.
